title: Decide a sufficient global balancing property for actual classes
statement: BAL(R,H) asserts for every actual-class pair x,y there are same-class u,v with u+v=x+y and coordinatewise |u-v|<=H. Using accepted effective global Presburger Psi_R, the sentence exists integer H>=0 forall x,y exists u,v [same-class implications and these linear constraints] is Presburger. Fixed-R precompilation decides it and computes H_R if true. For an abstract passing BAL(R,H_R) network use H_tilde=ceil(sqrt(d)*H_R); the multiset energy proof yields every feasible m in conv(Gamma intersect [m-H_tilde,m+H_tilde]^d); fixed nearby enumeration, exact membership and rational feasibility construct a mean-exact law with <=d+1 support and polynomial binary encoding/work. This source-conditional decision theorem is preserved. The separately supplied ROOT marked-coordinate proof now proves every actual SCC class passes, with its own strict-descent radius H. Failure of an abstract sufficient criterion would not itself be an inverse-calibration lower bound.

costs: Fixed Graver basis/normal forms, fixed R quantifier elimination, and any class-identity certification are finite computable precompilation costs. H_Lambda=sum signed Graver infinity norms is fixed; nearby witness enumeration at most(2H+2)^d, fixed-size rational feasibility and O_R(L)-bit populations/weights give poly_R(L) work. Modular inverse has O_R(L)-bit scalar brackets/activities and O_R(L) bisections with paid DDB1 moment error margins. BAL-certified reference lambda0=m+1 has conditioning probability>=2^-c_R(1+L) and witness KL<=c_R(1+L); regularization gives NUMERICAL radius O_R((L+1)/epsilon) and selector cost poly_R(L+epsilon^-1). epsilon^-1 may be exponential in input length, so this does not close unrestricted polynomial-BINARY accuracy. No source algorithms/checkers executed by Capital.
